note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“And the famine was sore in the land.” There have always been famines. The only difference now is that we think a famine could never happen, because we have grown accustomed to living here.

Luke records one: “there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cesar.” It did not come to pass the moment Agabus signified it. He had it under Caligula; Caligula was put to death, and Claudius came in, some five to ten years later, and then the dearth came.

That is said for a reason. We are telling our people famine is coming, and some are preparing while some are not. The word does not fail just because it does not happen the next day. In Genesis 43 the corn from Egypt was eaten up, and Jacob had to send his sons back, Benjamin with them, with Judah saying, “that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.” The famine came, as Joseph said it would.

precepts.why:
Ezra explains why famines come: “Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be always mindful of the scourges.”

Scourges come, like what happened with George Floyd among us, and 9/11. But our people tend to forget. Civil rights came around 1964 and 1965, 62 years ago, and people said it could never happen again, the same way people in South Africa act like apartheid never happened. Now they are bringing back vagrancy laws under the 13th Amendment, where the homeless get arrested and prison labor becomes slavery again. They are redrawing district lines, as with the Texas map that moves Representative Jasmine Crockett's home out of her district, so black representatives lose their seats and our people lose their voice in Congress.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.” While food is cheap and everybody thinks things are fine, supermarkets are being moved out of our communities and our people are being priced off the cruise lines and airlines. The evils are growing behind the scenes.

And nobody has solutions. Idi Amin expelled the Asian and European merchants from Uganda and handed their businesses to Ugandans who had no experience in the imports and exports, and the stores collapsed. South Africa today beats and drives out legal migrants from Ghana, Nigeria and the ECOWAS region who own small stores, while about 90 percent of the businesses and the land belong to white people: they turn against their own brothers while the real owners of the country stand in front of them. Black people in America burn down stores in our own neighborhoods instead of saving our money and opening our own, and the white man's solution is jail time.

“For many of them that dwell upon earth shall perish of famine; and the other, that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.” The Bible is telling you famine is coming upon the earth, even though people say, never in America. Egypt had its famine in Joseph's day, and it will come again.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Isaiah gives the rule for what belongs in the word of God: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate.” No prophecy shall fail, and every scripture has its mate. You cannot mate another book with the Bible.

Esau is now loading the Bible apps with additional books. Not the Apocrypha, which we read, but books like Enoch and Jasher. Read Jasher's account of the very events of Genesis 43 and 44, and it sounds strange, because it didn't happen that way: Judah threatening to slay all Egypt, throwing a stone of 400 shekels up to the heavens and sitting on it until it turned to dust, and Joseph's son Manasseh doing the same, when Manasseh and Ephraim were only little children at that time.

In Genesis the brothers go down to Egypt because of the famine, Judah pledges himself for Benjamin, “I will be surety for him,” and every piece of the story lines up with the rest of scripture. Jasher has no mate in the book of the Lord. That is why we stay away from those books.

precepts.text: The great city is Babylon the Great, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. This isn't the real Sodom or the real Egypt; it is a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt. On the dollar bill you have the pyramid with 1776 at the bottom, Novus Ordo Seclorum, and the obelisk stands in Washington. America knows this is a spiritual Egypt where they have captured tribes of Israel. And our Lord was crucified in Jerusalem; those same spirits that hated and murdered Christ are here again. They hate his image and they hate his teachings.
precepts.point: You had your 62 years since civil rights, and what have we done in those years? The same thing South Africans have done since apartheid ended in 1994. We have not organized into any faction of society; we still don't have our own hospitals, and we gave up the bus lines and institutions we did have in order to integrate. Now Esau is taking the integration rules and laws away.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
When Joseph saw Benjamin, “his bowels did yearn upon his brother,” and he went into his chamber and wept. Then he washed his face and said, “Set on bread.” They set on for Joseph by himself, for his brethren by themselves, and for the Egyptians by themselves, “because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

That is here as evidence that America is Egypt. John wrote: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The great city is Babylon the Great. It is not the real Sodom or the real Egypt; it is spiritually Sodom and spiritually Egypt. On the dollar bill you have the pyramid with 1776 at the bottom and Novus Ordo Seclorum, New World Order; the obelisk stands in Washington, D.C. America knows it is a spiritual Egypt where tribes of Israel are held captive.

And like ancient Egypt, it counted eating with the Hebrews an abomination. In the Jim Crow era it was an abomination for Esau to sit with us or let us sit in their restaurants. The signs read: we serve whites only, no Spanish or Mexicans; no dogs and no Mexicans, El Paso, Texas, 1929; and across the South we were forbidden their restaurants, their toilets, even their water fountains. Issachar was included in that too, no matter how light their skin; afterwards many Mexicans petitioned to be classified as white, because they had been classified as Negroes. This is not only ancient history; it was just over 60 years ago.

We have had our 62 years since civil rights, and what have we done with them? The same as South Africa since apartheid ended in 1994: nothing. We have not organized; we still have no hospitals of our own, and we gave up the bus lines and institutions we had in order to integrate. Now Esau is taking the integration laws away.

And “where also our Lord was crucified”: our Lord was crucified in Jerusalem, so this is a spiritual Jerusalem as well. The same spirits that hated and murdered Christ are back again here, in Babylon the Great. They hate his image, and they hate his teachings.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
In Exodus 1 the new king says “the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we: Come on, let us deal wisely with them.” The Egyptians were tall and strong, yet they said the Hebrews were mightier; something had happened for them to know it. They could not destroy us head on, so they set up institutions of oppression to keep us beneath them. There is nothing new under the sun, and Jim Crow was already around in Joseph’s time.

Genesis 43:32: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

Joseph had status. He was second over Egypt, the governor, the vizier, and still he was not granted the privileges of a full-blooded Egyptian. His Egyptian servants could not sit with him; they had their own table and he had his. He was a resource they could use, because his God gave him the dreams that kept them from famine, but he could not sit at their table because he was a Hebrew. It was an abomination for an Egyptian to eat with a Hebrew.

That is Jim Crow: Egyptians sit here, Hebrews sit there; whites sit here, coloreds sit there. The same people who used Joseph’s wisdom kept him apart, and the same thinking later dealt wisely with us in Egypt and in America.

precepts.why:
“And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” Our forefathers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery. He gained status in Egypt, Egypt got through the famine by his counsel, and now his brothers came to Egypt to buy food.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph had been a German Jew, or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him: a white man in Egyptian clothes stands out among Egyptians, because the Egyptians are black. They could not recognize their brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, looking like an Egyptian. “for he spake unto them by an interpreter”: he acted the part, speaking Egyptian so they would not know him. Joseph passed for an African, a black man, just as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were dark ancestors.

Then Genesis 43:32, at the meal: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. The Hebrews sat over there and the Egyptians over here, because them sitting together was an abomination. Israel had its own land, Goshen, and Egypt was apart. It was still segregation, even though both were dark: same color, different nation.

The pictures shown from the history books said the same. The Egyptians are brown. The Israelites working in the granary under a taskmaster have afros. Pharaoh is black, and Tutankhamun is black. Nefertiti is black as hell, and the Nubians are black as hell. The sacrifice of Isaac in the mosaic of the Beth Alpha synagogue shows Abraham and Isaac as black. The sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, are all dark; we fought the Canaanites in the land, and they are black too.

Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way. Jethro's daughters said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. Moses married an Ethiopian woman, a daughter of Ham, and a Hamite would have known a white man was no Egyptian. Even Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew only because he was circumcised, since both peoples were black.

precepts.text: They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search; the oppressor studies the former kingdoms and follows their blueprint.
precepts.point: Esau patterns himself after the former kingdoms. He learns how to govern and oppress by studying the kingdoms that were before him: ancient Babylon, ancient Greece, ancient Rome, ancient Egypt. They search out iniquities and accomplish a diligent search; nothing they do is accidental, everything follows the blueprint of the kingdoms that came before them.

note.label: Genesis 43: Benjamin Brought Down to Egypt

precepts.why:
“They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them? They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.” Nothing the oppressor does is accidental. Esau searches out iniquities; he learns how to govern and oppress by studying the kingdoms that were before him: ancient Babylon, ancient Greece, ancient Rome, ancient Egypt. Everything follows the blueprint of the kingdoms that came before.

That is why what was in Egypt showed up again in America. “the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians”: Joseph set by himself, his brethren by themselves, the Egyptians by themselves. Back in the 1900s it was colored only and whites only, no seat at the same table. They fashioned themselves after ancient Egypt; a diligent search, and the blueprint followed.

precepts.text: Judah becomes surety for Benjamin, guaranteeing his safe return and willing to bear the blame forever.
precepts.point: A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger, Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth”. A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of.

Judah did exactly that for Benjamin: “And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones. I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever”. Judah becomes surety for Benjamin, guaranteeing his safe return and willing to bear the blame forever.

That is what surety is: the words of your mouth bind you for another man. Judah's word snared him to Benjamin's fate, and that is why Solomon says to go, humble yourself and make sure your friend, and deliver yourself.
